summary:
Field Notes of a Visitor is an interactive narrative game which brings the stories of space exploration to life. Set aboard the International Space Station, it follows an astronaut who awakens with no memory of who he is. Guided by LARS, a small station robot, he explores an archive of three extraordinary missions: Apollo 11's Eagle descent stage, the Opportunity rover, and the Ingenuity helicopter.

Instead of just telling players what these missions achieved, the game lets them experience some of the challenges behind them. From handling computer overload during Apollo 11 to managing Opportunity's dwindling power and navigating Mars with Ingenuity, each mission puts players in the middle of real problems faced by NASA engineers. 

beyond the gameplay and the mystery, the game is about something bigger: what happens to a mission after it ends? Eagle never returned to Earth. Opportunity eventually fell silent on Mars. Ingenuity made its final flight, and someday, the ISS too will become a part of history. Yet none of these missions have really been forgotten. They left behind discoveries, lessons, and possibilities that continue to shape how we explore space. Through this game, we wanted to bring these machines back into the spotlight and give their stories another chance to be heard.
details:
What is our game?
Field Notes of a Visitor is a narrative exploration game with three playable historical mission simulations. Players take the role of an astronaut with amnesia aboard the nearly retired ISS, guided by Lars, an assistant robot. As they explore the station, they enter archived simulations of Apollo 11, Opportunity and Ingenuity and learn how each mission overcame impossible limits. Along the way, real NASA history and engineering are taught through play, and the simulations provide a glimpse into the science that made the missions possible.


What benefits does our game have?

We hope to inspire young learners by turning NASA’s forgotten devices into interactive games rather than just facts in a textbook. By allowing players to step directly into the shoes of astronauts, the goal of our game is to raise awareness about the brave machines left behind on the Moon and Mars. Ultimately we want the players to understand how each piece of technology worked, why it was left behind, and how the discoveries it made continue to pave the way for future space exploration.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use to develop our project? 

To build this game, our team combined visual art with AI-assisted tools. Every character and spacecraft was carefully designed by hand using Figma to create a contemporary look for young learners. For the technical portion and the coding of the game, we used Claude Code to help structure the game’s design and help write the code, bringing our interactive ship exploration, dialogue bubbles, and minigames to life smoothly. Everything was built and tested on our team’s personal computers to ensure accessible gameplay across all devices.

How is our project creative?
Our project combines storytelling, space history and interactive gameplay to make learning about NASA missions more engaging. Instead of simply presenting facts, players experience real mission challenges while following a mystery of their own, connecting the past achievements of space exploration with a story that unfolds around them.

What factors did our team consider?
We designed this game primarily for a younger audience interested in space, specifically kids ages 10-14 while also giving the game accessible controls and an engaging story to make it enjoyable for all ages as well. Our main goal is to spread awareness about these three extremely important NASA missions whose technology still lies on the Moon and Mars today: the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent, the Opportunity rover on Mars, and the Ingenuity Mars helicopter.
